work.abstract_text: Extending Moothathu's progression-exclusion construction (2010), we answer the open Question 5.6 of Meddaugh and Stephens (arXiv:2509.04312v1, Section 5, p. 12; 2025) affirmatively by constructing a mixing, surjective binary forward subshift with neighborhood 2-shadowing and a nonempty clopen set containing no nonempty periodic set. The subshift forbids an all-one arithmetic progression of length p^2+3 and difference p, for each positive integer p. Two separated deletion masks from a quadratic-irrational rotation trace every sufficiently accurate pseudo-orbit. The same construction is not of quasi-finite type, giving a further affirmative example for Question 5.3 (Section 5, p. 11), and has no ordinary shadowing. The same conclusions hold for every progression-length function ell(p)>=3 with ell(p)/p tending to infinity, without a monotonicity assumption. Each of the two tracing points can trace at a syndetic set of times, despite failure of quasi-finite type.

work.title: Neighborhood two-shadowing for progression subshifts: an extension of Moothathu (2010) answering Meddaugh–Stephens, arXiv:2509.04312v1, Section 5, Question 5.6
